1.answer:
Dear Jenny,

Thank you for your email. It is so kind of you to plan a party for my birthday.

I would like to have the party at a small coffee shop near my house in District 3. It is quiet and cozy, and it has a private room upstairs. My friends and I often meet there at weekends, so it feels like a second home.

My birthday is on Friday, 4th December, but I usually work late on Fridays. How about holding the party on Saturday, 5th December, at 6 p.m.? Everyone can come after work and stay longer because we do not work the next day. If this time does not suit you, just let me know.

You really do not need to buy me anything. However, if I could choose, I would wish for an e-book reader. I love reading, but paper books are heavy to carry. With an e-book reader, I can read on the bus or after swimming at the weekend.

Thank you again for your help. I can't wait to see you at the party!

Best wishes,
Minh

2.answer:
Nowadays, many countries are using more green energy, such as solar power and wind power, instead of coal and oil. This change is popular, but not everyone agrees that it brings only benefits. In my opinion, green energy has both advantages and disadvantages, and this essay will discuss both sides.

On the one hand, green energy brings several important benefits. Firstly, it is much cleaner than fossil fuels. Solar panels and wind turbines do not produce smoke, so the air becomes cleaner and people have fewer health problems. Secondly, green energy helps to fight climate change because it releases very little carbon dioxide. In addition, sunlight and wind will never run out. For example, Ninh Thuan province in Vietnam has strong sunshine all year, so many solar farms have been built there. As a result, the country depends less on imported fuel, and local people have more jobs.

On the other hand, green energy also has some drawbacks. Firstly, the cost of building solar farms and wind farms is very high. Poorer countries may not have enough money to invest in this technology. Secondly, green energy is not always stable. Solar panels cannot produce electricity at night, and wind turbines stop when there is no wind. Therefore, countries still need expensive batteries or other power plants as a backup. Moreover, large solar farms need a lot of land, so some forests and farmland may disappear.

In conclusion, green energy is clean and will never run out, but it is expensive and not always reliable. I believe its benefits are greater than its drawbacks. Governments should continue to invest in green energy and support new technology to make it cheaper and more stable.
